summary: On-demand ephemeral audit bundle via audit-proxy (SAS) with redaction-policy matrix for scheduled 3rd-party pen test
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Payments Inc.) needs a timeboxed, cryptographically-verifiable audit bundle for a scheduled third-party penetration test that starts 2026-03-15. They require: an on-demand export of ordered audit events for a tenant scope (tenant_id provided), row-level redaction consistent with their supplied PII mapping matrix, a machine-readable manifest with HMAC-signed checkpoints for chain-of-custody, and a short-lived SAS (shared access signature) download link served by our audit-proxy for auditors to pull the bundle.

Impact:
- Customer cannot complete their external penetration test without the evidence bundle; regulatory deadline is fixed.
- High-risk for sales/contract milestone if delivery misses test date.

Environment:
- Redwood production region: us-east-1
- Tenant scope: tenant: acme-payments-prod
- Requested window: 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-01T23:59:59Z

Requested artifacts / acceptance criteria:
1) Compressed audit bundle (NDJSON + per-file UTF-8) containing ordered events for tenant scope and time window, includes event_type, timestamp, request_id, actor.id, actor.role, resource.id, action, and raw_payload (when not redacted).
2) A redaction-policy matrix applied to the export and documented in the manifest (CSV mapping of field -> redaction rule) matching Acme's supplied mapping (attached).
3) Manifest.json listing file checksums (sha256), HMAC signature over manifest (KID referencing rotating signing key), and incremental offsets to support resume/partial-replay.
4) Short-lived (72 hours) pre-authenticated download link (SAS-style) produced by audit-proxy with IP allowlist for auditor CIDR and timebox.
5) Verification instructions for how Acme's security team can validate checksums and HMAC chain-of-custody.

Steps to produce / reproduce request:
- Customer provided redaction mapping CSV and auditor CIDR block via secured ticket attachment.
- Support to coordinate with SRE to run export job using export-runbook template and audit-proxy to host SAS.

Attachments provided by customer:
- redaction-matrix-acme-2026-03-09.csv
- auditor-cidr.txt

Notes:
- Customer explicitly requested no plaintext storage in public buckets; bundle may be placed in encrypted internal bucket and delivered via pre-auth URL only.
- Customer asked for checksum/HMAC verification steps suitable for their compliance team (to be included in the manifest and README).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Maya Chen): Opened ticket after receiving request from Acme security lead (security@acme-payments.com). Attached their mapping CSV. Marking P1 due to fixed pen-test date.

2026-03-10 11:03 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Acknowledged. Will validate mapping against export schema and check availability of encrypted bucket and signing key. Tentative ETA for export job: 2026-03-12. Need confirmation of exact time window and whether to include API response bodies (requested to be redacted per mapping).

2026-03-10 13:45 - Acme Security (Jordan Blake): Confirmed time window and requested API response bodies be redacted per mapping; approves 72-hour SAS link and auditor CIDR 198.51.100.0/24. Asked that we include a step-by-step verification script for their auditors.

2026-03-11 08:22 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Found one schema field in mapping 'user.displayName' that does not match current audit schema (actual field 'user.name'). Requested clarifying CSV from customer. Submitted INT-4423 to track mapping normalization work.
2026-03-12 16:10 - Support (Maya Chen): Customer provided corrected mapping attached to ticket. Proceeding to run export per runbook and will post manifest and SAS link when ready.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Hypothesis: Export can be produced by existing tenant-export job with redaction plug-in; need to confirm redaction rules support conditional masking and tokenization requested by customer.

2026-03-11 - Finding: Current redaction module supports regex and fixed replacement, but not pseudonymization token rotation. For this request we will apply deterministic hash replacement with salt documented in manifest.

2026-03-11 - Finding: Signing key rotation policy requires explicit KID in manifest; SRE to use key version v2026-02-28 (HSM-backed) and include key metadata in manifest but not private key. INT-4423 opened for automated mapping normalization.
2026-03-12 - Risk: SAS URL edge-case where auditor client retries from different IPs; added note to allowlist additional CIDR if needed and included expirations and instructions to request extension.
resolution:
Workaround/fix provided: Generated export bundle and uploaded to encrypted internal S3 bucket in us-east-1. Applied redaction-policy matrix (deterministic SHA256-salt replacement for designated PII fields). Created manifest.json with per-file sha256 checksums and an HMAC-SHA256 signature using KID 'audit-sign-v2026-02-28'. Provided README with verification commands (openssl sha256, hmac verify script) and chain-of-custody notes.

Delivery method: Audit-proxy issued a pre-authenticated download link (SAS) valid for 72 hours starting 2026-03-12T20:00:00Z with auditor CIDR 198.51.100.0/24 allowed. Link and short instructions sent via secure channel to Acme security contact.

Follow-up items:
- INT-4423: Automate mapping normalization to avoid manual CSV corrections (assigned to DataInfra, target 2026-04-01).
- Product request: Add pseudonymization token rotation support in redaction module (feature request to product backlog).
- Security: Rotate signing key KID 'audit-sign-v2026-02-28' per policy on 2026-06-01; notify customers with outstanding bundles.

Ticket status: Resolved delivery; waiting for customer confirmation of verification. If customer requests extended SAS window or additional IP allowlist entries, reopen or create follow-up support ticket.
